key_insight: Frozen LLM embeddings can separate sentences by language even when their meanings match. The paper proposes removing language-related variation so embeddings better reflect meaning across languages.
problem_solved: Training-free text embedding methods have focused mainly on English, leaving multilingual performance underexplored and equivalent sentences misaligned across languages.
method: Systematically study multilingual text embeddings extracted from frozen LLMs.
Analyze language-conditioned embedding geometry to identify cross-language semantic misalignment.
Propose paired-residual subspace removal to reduce language-specific variation; implementation details are not available in the supplied, truncated abstract.
impact: This approach could improve multilingual semantic search, retrieval, and similarity matching without retraining the underlying LLM. The supplied abstract does not include results establishing the size of these benefits.
visual_elements: Before-and-after embedding maps: language-separated clusters versus meaning-aligned clusters.
Equivalent sentences in different languages connected by lines showing their embedding misalignment.
Conceptual pipeline: frozen LLM → embeddings → paired-residual subspace removal → aligned representations.
Locked-model icon emphasizing the training-free approach.
paper_title: Steering beyond Language: Improving Multilingual Training-Free Text Embeddings via Paired-Residual Subspace Removal
paper_authors: Ailiang Lin, Zhuoyun Li, Yusong Wang, Keyu Mao, Kotaro Funakoshi
